title: A meta-analysis of AI-enabled personalized STEM education in schools
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the need for quantitative evidence on the effectiveness of AI-enabled personalized STEM education in K-12 schools. Prior reviews had largely been qualitative or focused on narrower technologies, leaving unclear the overall impact of AI-supported personalized learning and the conditions under which it works best. The study therefore asks how effective AI-enabled personalized STEM education is in schools and which moderator variables explain differences in outcomes.

The authors conducted a meta-analysis following PRISMA procedures, synthesizing 99 effect sizes from 32 randomized controlled trial studies published between 2012 and 2024. The review focused on AI-enabled personalized learning interventions in school STEM subjects and coded moderators including school level, AI application type, personalized learning model, outcome type, subject area, and whether generative AI was used. The included AI applications spanned intelligent tutoring systems, personalized educational games, AR/VR, and other AI-supported tools.

The population was K-12 students across multiple school levels, including kindergarten, elementary, junior high, and senior high school, in school-based STEM learning contexts worldwide. Because this is a meta-analysis, the paper aggregates evidence across many settings rather than reporting a single intervention site or country. The focus is explicitly on student learning outcomes in school STEM education.

The main conclusion is that AI-enabled personalized STEM education produces a statistically significant small-to-medium positive effect overall compared with non-AI approaches (reported overall g = 0.455). The strongest effects were found for junior and senior high school students, AR/VR-based tools, and more learner-centered models that combine AI with classroom or collaborative pedagogies. Effects also varied by subject, with comprehensive courses showing the largest gains. By contrast, observed outcome type and generative-AI versus non-generative-AI status did not significantly moderate effects. The authors argue for evidence-based, pedagogically aligned integration of AI in K-12 STEM education.

identified_tools.name: ITS (General)
identified_tools.description: Intelligent Tutoring Systems are AI-enabled instructional systems that adapt learning based on student models and cognitive or motivational states.
identified_tools.use_case: This meta-analysis synthesized RCTs of AI-enabled personalized STEM education in K-12 schools, with ITS as one major archetype among the included intervention types.

findings.finding_summary: Across 99 effect sizes from 32 randomized controlled trial studies of AI-enabled personalized K-12 STEM education, the overall pooled effect was small-to-medium and statistically significant (Hedges' g=0.455, 95% CI [0.327, 0.583], p<0.001). The paper treats ITS as a major AI application type within this broader evidence base rather than isolating one named product.
findings.measure: Student learning outcomes in personalized K-12 STEM education versus non-AI comparison conditions

findings.finding_summary: For the ITS subgroup, 61 effect sizes showed a small but statistically significant positive effect on K-12 STEM learning outcomes (g=0.347, p<0.001). The paper reports this as smaller than the AR/VR subgroup but still beneficial relative to non-AI conditions.
findings.measure: STEM learning outcomes for ITS-based personalized interventions

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Generative AI refers to AI systems based on generative models, such as transformer-based models, that can produce text, images, video, or other data.
identified_tools.use_case: The meta-analysis coded included studies as GAI-related versus GAI-unrelated to test whether generative AI-based personalized STEM tools produced different effects in K-12 settings.

findings.finding_summary: GAI-related tools showed a statistically significant positive effect on K-12 STEM learning outcomes (g=0.430, p<0.001). However, the moderator test found no significant difference between GAI-related and GAI-unrelated tools (QB=0.058, p=0.810).
findings.measure: STEM learning outcomes for GAI-related personalized interventions

quality_tier_rationale: This is a meta-analysis synthesizing 99 effect sizes from 32 randomized controlled trial studies, which fits the highest evidence tier. Some heterogeneity is high, but the design is still strong overall.
impact_tier_rationale: The pooled overall effect was g=0.455, which is a medium positive impact by the provided framework. Subgroup effects for ITS and GAI-related tools were also positive.
